task: Find why a READ-only alias of an implicit receiver field lacked checker ownership authority in methods.
observation: The ownership walk normalized an implicit receiver field place such as inner.frontier to storage root self, but the local ownership fact producer only proceeded when that root had a lexical binding identity. The checker accepted the source while generated Rust moved the field from a shared reference. Resolving the first receiver field to its declaration identity allowed the existing exact RHS fact to be retained without adding a fact class or changing the consumer.
impact: The failing native lowering now has a checker-owned READ fact at the alias RHS occurrence; the consume control still rejects with OWNERSHIP_ILLEGAL_CONSUME. Fast Debug and native acceptance remain unverified on the combined consumer checkpoint.
evidence: ./build/compiler/moss-dev run --interp tmp/method_field_read.moss (blocked by checked constructor declaration has no unique ObjectType)

resolution.summary: The checker now uses a stable receiver-field declaration identity to publish the existing local ownership fact. Combined native/Fast Debug validation is still required.
